rationale:
All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to abdominal aortic aneurysm), so selection hinges on comparative PRS-relevant evidence and study archetype rather than label match. PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (MVP/MAYO-VDB; Circulation) and reports a PRS-comparable effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), which is explicitly highlighted in the provided guidance as a strong predictor when AUC/R2 are missing. Most other candidates primarily report full-model discrimination (AUROC/C-index) without isolating PRS-only contribution, which the guidance warns should not be substituted for PRS performance; additionally, two are clearly framework/portability-style scores (PGS001784 from a global biobank framework; PGS002054 from a UKB portability sweep), which are penalized when disease-focused alternatives exist.

Runners-up: PGS003972 is the next best-supported disease-focused multi-cohort GWAS meta-analysis PRS-CS score (Nat Genet; many AAA cohorts listed), but its visible metric is only a full-model AUROC (0.69) with unknown covariates and no PRS-only metric/effect size, limiting comparability. PGS001784 is a methodologically strong PRS-CS-auto genome-wide score with an explicit PRS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2 (0.014661) on a very large EUR evaluation sample, but it is from a pan-trait/global-biobank framework paper and its PRS-only R2 is modest (and near the partial-r reported for PGS002054), so it ranks behind the disease-focused candidates.

Main limitation driving DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL: across the pool, PRS-only metrics are sparse/inconsistent (many full-model AUROCs with differing/unknown covariates), and the best candidate (PGS000753) is a sparse P+T score (29 variants) with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported, so the evidence does not cleanly identify a single clearly superior benchmark-transfer model. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target (alcohol dependence / alcohol use disorder / problematic alcohol use), but none reports PRS-only AUROC/R2; available metrics are limited to ΔR², OR(top 10% vs rest), and betas, making the choice somewhat uncertain.

PGS002738 is best supported because its phenotype alignment is the most direct (trait_efo="alcohol dependence", phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder"), it is developed in a disease-focused multi-cohort context (MVP + UKB), and it shows comparatively strong discriminative evidence via OR(top 10% vs rest)=1.96 (95% CI 1.54–2.51) in EUR evaluation (n=7,900). This OR magnitude is a stronger practical signal than the small ΔR² values reported by the UKB-only siblings.

Runners-up: PGS000201 and PGS000202 are from the same publication family with the same phenotyping_reported (DSM-5 criteria count, log-transformed) and EUR-only evaluation, but they are less directly labeled to alcohol dependence than AUD and show weaker performance evidence (ΔR² 0.01192 for PGS000201; 0.00456 for PGS000202). Between them, PGS000201 is preferred over PGS000202 due to higher ΔR², larger variant count, and larger validation sample (7,599 vs 1,251).

PGS002739 is deprioritized despite being AUD-labeled because its evaluation is AFR-only (African American or Afro-Caribbean) and it is a very sparse gene-based score (858 variants), making it less likely to rank highest in a generic benchmark setting absent explicit benchmark-ancestry alignment.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait via trait_efo=alcoholic liver cirrhosis, so a direct-match selection is possible. PGS000704 is best supported structurally: it uses a genome-wide snpnet multi-PRS approach with very large variant count (183,271) and large UKB development/validation (DEV EUR; EVAL EUR/MAE; validation n=135,300). Its reported discrimination is only a full-model C-index/AUROC-like metric (0.711) with basic covariates (age as time scale, sex, batch, PCs), plus a modest HR per SD (1.18), so the PRS-only contribution is unclear—this limits confidence and prevents a high-quality designation. As runners-up, PGS001777 has a small 3-variant score but shows strong effect-size-style separation (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18) and reports AUROC 0.671; however, it has unknown covariates and a small validation sample (n=1,390) with a phenotyping note restricted to males, reducing expected benchmark transfer. PGS004913 is disease-focused and endpoint-aligned with clean basic covariates, but is a small PRSice-2 score (20 variants) with only modest reported R² (0.029) and no AUROC, making it harder to justify over the more structurally powerful genome-wide model. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo matches), but most are from framework-style or benchmarking contexts with limited PRS-comparable metrics, making the choice non-definitive. PGS001262 is preferred because it has strong endpoint fidelity (doctor-diagnosed angina in phenotyping_reported), reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.58683; PGS R2 no covariates=0.01304) that are plausible relative to the provided EUR h2_obs ceiling (~0.009–0.014 range depending on definition) and includes incremental AUROC (0.0098), indicating measurable PRS contribution beyond basic covariates. The main limitation is that it comes from the pan-trait UKB '813 traits' sparse snpnet framework family, which domain guidance flags as often underperforming in external validation despite complete metadata; additionally, its very high full-model AUROC (0.807) is likely covariate-driven and not directly comparable. Runners-up: PGS001261 (time-to-event angina pectoris) has slightly lower PRS-only metrics (PGS R2=0.01228) and a time-to-event endpoint penalty but otherwise similar evidence; PGS001260 (angina) is similar but with the weakest PRS-only metrics among these three (PGS R2=0.01185). Other candidates (e.g., PGS004527/PGS004457 with ORs, and the MVP method-comparison set PGS00504x/PGS00505x with C-index/OR) lack clear PRS-only metrics or have missing training details in this context, so they are harder to justify as the single best benchmark-transfer choice from visible evidence alone.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, so a direct-match exists. For likely external-benchmark transfer, the strongest visible structural signal is PGS002089: it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with a large variant count (22,026), and it comes from a UKB portability framework where it was evaluated across multiple ancestry groups (EUR/GME/SAS), which is supportive of robustness. However, its performance evidence is limited to partial correlation (partial-r=0.0919) with no PRS-only AUROC/R² reported, lowering certainty.

Runner-up PGS001267 is supported by explicit PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC (0.7265) and PGS-only R² (0.0988) with basic covariates and multi-ancestry evaluation; but it is a very sparse snpnet model (10 variants) from a pan-trait UKB framework paper, which domain guidance flags as often less transferable. Runner-up PGS001876 is another UKB portability-framework direct AS score with a larger training sample and a reasonable partial-r (0.0797), but it is a smaller penalized-regression score (85 variants) and has weaker reported partial-r than PGS002089. The Taiwanese EAS-only models (PGS003420–PGS003424) report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and small validation (n=1,298), so their AUROC is not reliably comparable as PRS-only evidence for benchmark ranking.

Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254, PGS005255, PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported because it is an exact trait match with endpoint-fidelity phenotyping (“Incident aortic stenosis cases”), uses a strong genome-wide method (LDPred2) with very large variant count (~1.12M), and has the strongest visible effect-size evidence among the direct AS models (HR=1.92) plus a reported full-model C-index=0.87 in a large EUR evaluation (n=446,895). Main limitation: the reported discrimination is full-model (with multiple clinical covariates), and no PGS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be cleanly compared.

Runners-up: PGS005254 is also an exact aortic stenosis PRS with genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS), large variant count (~1.11M), and moderate HR=1.64 (CI provided), but lacks any AUC/R² and has smaller validation (n=244,450). Between the remaining two, PGS005255 and PGS005256 have identical method/variant count/covariates/validation size and similar HR=1.53; PGS005255 is ranked slightly ahead only because its trait_reported (“Mean pressure gradient”) is marginally closer to stenosis severity than “Peak aortic velocity,” though both are still evaluated on incident aortic stenosis and are effectively near-tied given the visible metadata. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including PGS001135 ("Arthritis (nos)", trait_efo=arthritis) and two Commun Biol models explicitly mapped to arthritis (PGS004477 and PGS004547; both "M13 (Other arthritis)", trait_efo=arthritis). PGS001135 is the most endpoint-faithful generic arthritis model in the list with PRS-comparable metrics reported (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.53928; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00291) and standard/basic covariates, and its PRS-only R2 is below the provided arthritis heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0009; h2_liability=0.0610), so it passes the sanity-check framing. The main limitation is that PGS001135 comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused models in external validation; however, among the visible same-trait (arthritis) options, the Commun Biol arthritis models provide only effect-size summaries (OR~1.20–1.26) without PRS-only AUROC/R2 and have unknown covariates, making their standalone PRS performance harder to benchmark. As runners-up, PGS004547 is preferred over PGS004477 because it reports a larger OR (1.262 vs 1.196) within the same publication family and endpoint label, with PGS004477 next. Confidence is moderate because the direct-match set is small and the best candidate is framework-derived while the alternatives lack comparable PRS-only metrics.

All listed candidates are direct matches to asthma, so selection hinges on endpoint fidelity plus PRS-comparable performance evidence and study archetype. PGS002727 (PRS-CS; multiancestral pediatric asthma) has the strongest directly PRS-informative effect-size evidence in the visible set (OR=1.57 per SD) and very large evaluation support (n=391,820) with multi-ancestry evaluation, which together suggest robust external transfer despite covariates being unknown. Runner-up PGS001782 (PRS-CS-auto; Global Biobank/Cell Genom) has solid PRS-comparable evidence (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.048844; AUROC 0.659) and a disease-focused multi-biobank training context, but is a framework-style score and shows weaker effect-size evidence than PGS002727. Second runner-up PGS002061 (LDpred2; UKB portability framework) has the best partial correlation among the portability siblings (partial-r=0.1184) with a strong genome-wide shrinkage method, but lacks explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 and comes from a portability framework, making its benchmark transfer advantage less certain. Overall confidence is limited because many candidates report only full-model metrics (often non-comparable across covariate sets), and the apparent high AUROC in some records (e.g., childhood asthma PGS002248) is likely covariate-driven and/or endpoint-restricted, so it is not reliable as standalone PRS evidence for generic asthma.

All 6 candidates are direct EFO matches to atopic eczema, but several have endpoint mismatches (paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis: PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903) that reduce endpoint fidelity for generic atopic eczema risk. Among the remaining endpoint-faithful options, PGS002755 and PGS004587 both target incident atopic dermatitis with similar covariates and very large EUR evaluation (n=337,910) and report comparable HR (high vs low PRS) evidence; PGS002755 is preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants, which is structurally more likely to capture polygenic signal than the 23-variant GWAS-hits score in PGS004587. PGS001773 reports a very high full-model AUROC/R², but these are full-model (not PRS-only) metrics and the endpoint is restricted to moderate-to-severe AD in Canadian cohorts with a small validation (n=676) and non-basic covariates (parental ethnicity), making the apparent performance less comparable and potentially covariate-driven; it remains the next best runner-up after the two incident-AD models. Overall confidence is limited because none of the leading candidates provides PRS-only AUROC/R², and the strongest-looking AUC evidence is full-model and on a narrower severity phenotype.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (atrial fibrillation) by trait_reported/trait_efo, so ranking hinges on endpoint fidelity, PRS-comparable evidence, covariate comparability, and study archetype. PGS005168 is best supported because it is a disease-focused, large multi-cohort AF meta-analysis score (many AF cohorts listed) with a direct AF endpoint and only modest clinical covariate packaging (CHARGE-AF included, but alongside basic demographics), and it reports a strong per-SD effect size (HR=1.6663) plus a high C-index (0.8718) in European evaluation; the effect size provides PRS-discrimination evidence even though the C-index is likely full-model. Runner-up PGS005313 is also disease-focused and multi-cohort with a strong OR (1.82) and AUROC=0.78, but it is evaluated in a MAE-only setting and provides less breadth/replication evidence in the visible fields than PGS005168. Second runner-up PGS002814 has very large upstream GWAS scale and strong reported OR (~1.94) with AUROC=0.74, but it is explicitly East-Asian–anchored (GWAS/DEV MAE; EVAL EAS), making it less likely to top a generic external benchmark without knowing the benchmark ancestry. Main limitation: across top candidates, most reported AUROC/C-index values appear to be full-model (often with covariates), and explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 is generally absent, so confidence is reduced and the choice relies heavily on disease-focused multi-cohort design plus per-SD effect sizes. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct matches by concept (atrial flutter is explicitly present in trait_reported/trait_efo for all, either alone or combined with atrial fibrillation). PGS001263 is preferred because it is the only candidate with an exact atrial flutter endpoint label and it reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.617 and PGS-only R2=0.025) plus incremental AUROC, enabling more reliable PRS-only comparison than the portability-study models that report only partial-r. Its PRS-only R2 is also below the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443), so it is not obviously implausible. Main limitation: PGS001263 (and PGS001339) come from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming in external validation; additionally, the strongest-looking AUROC shown is full-model and likely covariate-influenced, so it should not be over-weighted. Runners-up: PGS001339 is very similar (same framework, similar PRS-only AUROC/R2) but has a less specific combined AF+flutter time-to-event phenotype, which is a mild endpoint-fidelity penalty versus the exact flutter label. Between the two portability-study options, PGS002050 is ranked above PGS001841 because it shows slightly higher partial-r (0.1034 vs 0.1026) with otherwise matched endpoint/covariates/publication context, though both lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 which keeps confidence moderate rather than high.

Two direct-match candidates are visible (both map to autism spectrum disorder), but only one has strong endpoint fidelity. PGS000327 has coherent phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported = Autism spectrum disorder; trait_reported/efo also ASD), comes from an ASD-focused GWAS meta-analysis context (Nat Genet), and provides supportive PRS signal via effect size (OR per SD = 1.33) plus a higher reported R² metric (0.0245) than the alternative; covariates are basic (genetic PCs, genotyping wave). PGS002790 is a weaker direct-match despite the ASD label because phenotyping_reported is explicitly mismatched/withdrawn (Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)), and its reported partial R² is lower (~0.0055) with no effect-size support; its study framing is broader (sex-specific cross-disorder associations), making endpoint fidelity and transfer to an ASD benchmark less certain. Overall outcome is sub-optimal because neither model reports clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics (e.g., PGS-only AUROC/R²), and the selected R² fields appear to be full-model/partial metrics rather than explicitly PRS-only, limiting certainty about benchmark ranking.

All 20 candidates are direct matches to basal cell carcinoma by trait_efo, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and strength of PRS-specific evidence. PGS000452 is best supported because it has clean phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: Basal cell carcinoma), basic covariates only (age/sex/batch/PCs), and the strongest visible PRS-discrimination signals among the comparable PRSweb cancer-family models: high per-SD OR=1.663 (>=1.5 is strong per provided guidance) plus strong top-1% vs rest OR=3.61, alongside one of the highest reported full-model AUROCs (0.632) within the same covariate-light setting. The two closest runners-up are PGS000454 and PGS000456, which share the same endpoint/covariate structure and have essentially the same full-model AUROC (~0.63) and similarly strong per-SD ORs (~1.66 and ~1.63, respectively); they remain strong alternatives but are slightly less supported than PGS000452 based on marginally weaker/less consistent effect-size package. Confidence is Moderate because many candidates are near-clones with very similar metrics and none report clearly PRS-only AUROC/R2, so small AUROC differences are not decisive and ranking relies heavily on effect sizes within a single study family. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept via trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. PGS002032 and PGS001824 are the cleanest endpoint matches (both: "Disorders of bilirubin excretion"), come from the same portability study family, share the same covariates and reported partial-r (0.0716), and have identical training cohort context (UKB) and ancestry distribution; between them, PGS002032 is structurally preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far more variants (19,768 vs 22), which is generally a positive signal for external performance when other evidence is tied. PGS001824 is the closest runner-up because it is otherwise indistinguishable on endpoint and reported metric but uses a more sparse penalized regression with very low variant count. PGS000924 is ranked third despite having explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.88697; PGS-only R2 0.21843) because it is a pan-trait sparse UKB framework score ("across 813 traits"; snpnet with only 5 variants) and uses a time-to-event endpoint, both of which are warning signals for external transfer; additionally, its reported PGS-only R2 exceeds the provided local heritability estimate (h2_obs=0.0889), raising comparability/sanity-check concerns. Overall confidence is limited because the two top candidates lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (only partial-r is provided), making the best-vs-runner-up distinction rely mainly on structural method/variant-count signals.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait family (bipolar disorder) and share the same publication, method (SDPR), training cohort (PGC), and EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, so there is no clear study-design or transportability differentiator in the visible metadata. Endpoint fidelity is weak/ambiguous across the set because each model’s phenotyping_reported is a non-diagnosis behavioral/cognitive measure (e.g., pattern comparison; DSM5 depression; sluggish cognitive tempo) rather than a bipolar disorder case-control/diagnosis endpoint, which limits confidence for a bipolar-disorder benchmark. With no PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and only small full_model partial R² values reported (all ~0.0025–0.0031, likely reflecting association with the reported non-diagnosis phenotypes), performance evidence is not strongly discriminative. Given the target is broad ‘bipolar disorder’, PGS002786 is preferred on concept alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo exactly bipolar disorder rather than subtype I/II), while PGS002787 and PGS002788 are the closest runners-up as subtype-specific variants with otherwise near-identical evidence.

All three candidates are direct matches under the provided query context, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and in how informative their performance evidence is for external benchmarking. PGS002034 and PGS001826 share the same reported phenotype ("Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)") and come from the same UKB portability framework paper; between these siblings, PGS002034 is structurally favored because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far more variants (32,552 vs 45) while showing essentially identical partial-correlation performance (0.0563 vs 0.0562) under the same covariate set and validation context—making PGS002034 the most likely to transfer better in a hidden benchmark given no stronger, disease-focused alternative is visible. PGS001826 is the closest runner-up as the near-clone sibling with nearly identical endpoint and performance evidence but weaker structural properties (penalized regression with very sparse variant set). PGS001033 is ranked third despite having explicit AUROC/R2 fields because it is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework ("across 813 traits"), is extremely sparse (1 variant), and uses a time-to-event phenotype; per the provided domain guidance, such framework sparse models tend to generalize poorly and full-model AUROC should not be over-weighted. Overall confidence is only Moderate because none of the candidates provides strong, clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics across independent external cohorts, and two of the three are from a portability/framework archetype rather than a disease-focused multi-cohort study. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All selected models are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = breast carcinoma; phenotyping_reported = Breast cancer) and come from the same disease-endpoint benchmarking study family ("Evaluation of polygenic scoring methods in five biobanks..."), which provides a coherent cluster of comparable, endpoint-faithful candidates. Within that cluster, PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has the strongest reported discrimination and variance explained in the visible evidence (full_model_auc=0.6625; full_model_r2=0.0764) with covariates explicitly set to 0, reducing concern that performance is driven by clinical covariates rather than the PRS. The two runners-up are the next-best supported siblings by the same criteria: PGS004040 (LDpred2.CV; full_model_auc=0.6598; full_model_r2=0.0739) and PGS004025 (LDpred2-auto; full_model_auc=0.6598; full_model_r2=0.0736), both also with covariates=0 and similar endpoint/ancestry context. Confidence is Moderate because these are full-model metrics (not explicitly PGS-only AUROC/R2), and several other direct-match candidates exist outside this family (e.g., older disease-focused PRS and other biobank-derived scores) but lack directly comparable PRS-only metrics in the provided context, limiting certainty about external benchmark ranking.

All 10 visible candidates are direct matches to celiac disease via trait_efo, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS000316 is preferred because it targets an unqualified coeliac disease endpoint (phenotyping_reported matches the target), comes from a disease-focused clinical-care context (not a pan-trait/portability sweep), and shows strong discrimination evidence (AUROC=0.879 with CI) in European validation; while this AUROC is a full-model metric (covariates listed as Unknown), it is still supportive and not obviously a framework artifact. Runner-up PGS000040 is also disease-focused with a direct coeliac disease endpoint and reports very high AUROC=0.9, but it is likewise full-model only with unknown covariates and smaller training/validation than PGS000316, making its apparent edge less reliable for benchmark transfer. Second runner-up PGS002067 has a clean direct endpoint and a methodologically strong genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with multi-ancestry evaluation context, but it reports only partial correlation (partial-r=0.1241) rather than PRS-only AUROC/R², limiting comparability and making it harder to justify over the disease-focused AUROC-supported models. Overall confidence is moderate because the strongest-looking AUCs are full-model (PGS-only metrics are largely missing), and several candidates come from known framework/portability papers (PGS001301, PGS001856/1894/2067/2107) which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused models in external benchmarks. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). The strongest structural signal is PGS003428: it is a disease-focused cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis-derived genome-wide shrinkage score (LDpred; ~2.9M variants) with an incident endpoint and basic covariates (age, smoking), which domain guidance suggests tends to transfer better than sparse/framework scores or small GWAS-hit sets when endpoint fidelity is comparable. However, the visible performance evidence is limited and mostly full-model C-index (0.613) plus HR=1.33, with no PRS-only AUROC/R2, so confidence is capped.

Runners-up: PGS000073 and PGS000784 are near-clone 10-variant GWAS-significant scores evaluated in large European cohorts with similar covariates and similar effect sizes (HR~1.21–1.22) and full-model discrimination (~0.745 AUROC/C-index). They are supported by coherent endpoint/covariate alignment and large evaluation, but their small variant count and reliance on full-model metrics (not PRS-only) make them less likely to be the top standalone PRS in an external benchmark than a genome-wide shrinkage score. PGS001299 is penalized as a pan-trait UKB sparse framework model (snpnet; 24 variants) with weak PRS-only AUROC (~0.55) and tiny PGS R2; PGS003389 shows weak full-model AUROC (~0.563); PGS005165 is EAS-only (GWAS/EVAL) with modest C-index (~0.566), making it less broadly supported absent a specified benchmark ancestry.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis (some via ICD10 K80 or a closely related composite endpoint including cholecystitis). The strongest visible, PRS-comparable performance evidence among endpoint-faithful models comes from the UKB portability study siblings PGS001861/PGS002072, which report partial correlation in European validation; between them, PGS002072 is slightly better supported due to the higher partial-r (0.098 vs 0.0948) and use of a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (428,587), which is structurally favorable for polygenic traits. As runners-up, PGS001861 remains close (same endpoint/covariates/ancestry context but slightly lower partial-r and a more sparse penalized regression), and PGS001174 is next-best because it provides explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.623 and PGS-only R2 0.028) plus incremental AUROC, with values that are plausible under the provided EUR heritability ceiling (h2_obs 0.0214; liability 0.1372), though it is penalized as a pan-trait sparse UKB framework score and uses a time-to-event phenotype. Confidence is not high because the most structurally modern disease-specific ICD10 K80 models (PGS004476/PGS004546) and the EAS-focused PRS-CSx model (PGS005150) lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and provide only modest effect-size summaries (OR~1.22–1.30; beta reported without clear scale), making cross-candidate benchmarking uncertain.

All listed candidates are direct matches to chronic kidney disease by trait_efo, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable evidence. PGS002237 is best supported because it comes from a disease-focused CKD paper (Nat Med: “Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries”), uses a clear CKD stage 3+ style endpoint (eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2), has large development (n=279,819), multi-ancestry evaluation, and shows a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.47) consistent with meaningful PRS signal; its reported AUROC=0.78 is full-model and covariate-heavy, so it is discounted but still compatible with a strong underlying PRS. Runners-up: among the coherent 2023 AJHG five-biobank CKD-or-dialysis cluster (same endpoint family, covariates=0, same dev n=13,496, same eval n=90,274), PGS004158 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) is structurally favored because it is an explicit multi-PRS ensemble and has the highest full-model AUROC (0.5917) and R² (0.01996) within that cluster; next is PGS004045 (LDpred2.CV) as the strongest single-method sibling with near-top AUROC/R². Confidence is Moderate because (i) PGS002237 lacks PRS-only AUROC/R² and uses heavy clinical covariates, limiting comparability, and (ii) the five-biobank cluster has cleaner covariates but materially lower reported discrimination, making cross-study ranking uncertain from visible fields alone.

All 10 candidates are direct matches via trait_efo=chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, but they split into multiple study archetypes with different endpoint instantiations and metric comparability. PGS001783 is preferred because it is a direct COPD endpoint with a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092) plus a reported AUROC=0.74, and it comes from a broad multi-biobank development context (many cohorts listed) using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) rather than a sparse pan-trait UKB framework. Its PRS-comparable R2 is also below the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.0388), passing the sanity check. Main limitation: the evaluation is EUR-only with small validation n=7,128 and the AUROC is not explicitly labeled as PGS-only, so cross-model comparability remains imperfect.

Runners-up: PGS004536 is a direct COPD ICD code endpoint (J44) and uses an explicit multi-score aggregation method (RFDiseasemetaPRS), with a moderate-to-strong per-SD OR=1.4876 (supportive when AUC/R2 are missing), but it lacks comparable PRS-only metrics and has unknown covariates. PGS001788 is another PRS-CS-auto multi-biobank COPD score with very large validation n=337,168 and AUROC=0.715, but its PRS-comparable R2 is materially lower (0.0163) than PGS001783, making it less likely to top an external benchmark if the R2 reflects true PRS signal.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to the target disease concept (cirrhosis of liver), but several are alcohol-specific or have endpoint/covariate limitations, and none reports clearly PRS-only AUROC/R2 (so full-model AUROC/C-index is not directly comparable as standalone PRS performance). ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency
rationale: Direct-match candidates are present (both map to the target EFO and share the same reported/phenotyped endpoint: “Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”). Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to corneal dystrophy with matching trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported) and come from the same UKB portability publication with the same training cohort (UKB), training N (391,124), covariates (basic demographics + PCs), and the same reported validation sample size (19,321) and ancestry distribution. All listed candidates are direct matches at the EFO level (coronary artery disease), but many have endpoint/covariate packaging or lack PRS-comparable metrics, making the best choice non-unique from visible evidence.

Best pick (PGS003725): strongest overall combination of (i) endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: coronary artery disease), (ii) modern genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with substantial variant count (1,296,172), and (iii) strong PRS signal via effect sizes (OR=2.14; HR=1.75). Runner-up 1 (PGS002244): also a direct CAD endpoint with a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred; 6,576,338 variants) and strong effect size evidence (OR=1.64). It has broad multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/SAS), but lacks the very strong OR/HR magnitudes shown for PGS003725 in the visible record.

Runner-up 2 (PGS000013): direct CAD endpoint, genome-wide shrinkage (LDpred; 6,630,150 variants), and it uniquely reports a PRS-comparable metric (pgs_only_r2=0.04), which is below the provided CAD liability h2 ceiling (0.1323) and thus sanity-consistent. However, its visible PRS-only evidence is still limited (no PRS-only AUROC; reliance on full-model AUROC=0.81) and it is older than the multi-ancestry LDpred2 CAD score family.

Main limitation driving DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL: key candidates report only full-model AUROC/C-index (often non-comparable across differing covariates), and several high full-model AUROCs (e.g., PGS001780 AUROC=0.913; PGS000018 AUROC=0.89) are likely heavily covariate-driven or endpoint-specific, while PRS-only metrics are largely absent—so the benchmark-top model cannot be identified with high certainty from the visible fields alone.

All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease (trait_efo aligns; phenotyping_reported is Crohn’s disease for PGS001331/PGS004254 and a time-to-event Crohn endpoint for PGS001330). PGS001331 is preferred because it provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.579 and PGS-only R² 0.00677) plus incremental AUROC (0.027) under basic covariates, and it has the strongest PRS-only metrics among the two near-clone snpnet framework siblings (PGS001331 > PGS001330 on PGS-only AUROC/R² and full-model AUROC). Overall confidence is moderate (not high) because the best-supported PRS-comparable evidence comes from a pan-trait UKB framework family (known to generalize less well), while the more disease-focused-looking alternative lacks PRS-only metrics in the visible record. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (dementia) are present, including multiple models with trait_efo=dementia and/or phenotyping_reported indicating incident all-cause dementia. PGS005170 is best supported because it has the strongest endpoint fidelity to the target (phenotyping_reported: incident all-cause dementia; trait_reported: all-cause dementia; trait_efo: dementia) and a structurally strong method (integrative PRS combining 24 component PRSs; >1.3M variants), which domain guidance flags as a consistent positive predictor of external performance (multi-score aggregation). It also reports a reasonable full-model AUROC (0.761) and an HR (1.25), with only basic covariates plus APOE alleles, supporting that the PRS contributes signal.

Runners-up: (1) PGS000823 has strong endpoint fidelity (incident all-cause dementia) in a disease-focused cohort-study context and reports a supportive HR contrast (top vs bottom third HR=1.36), but lacks PRS-comparable metrics and uses a smaller GWAS-hit SNP set (23 variants). (2) PGS004281 is an exact dementia endpoint (all-cause dementia) with a large UKB-based evaluation and reports a high full-model AUROC (~0.819), but it is a single-paper method-focused score with no PRS-only metrics shown, making it harder to compare PRS contribution and thus less reliably benchmark-transferable than the integrative dementia-specific model.

Main limitation: across the candidate set, PRS-only metrics are largely missing for the strongest endpoint-faithful dementia models, so the choice relies heavily on endpoint fidelity + method-family signals rather than directly comparable PRS-only AUC/R2; this keeps confidence below High.

All listed candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (depressive disorder / major depressive disorder), but many have endpoint or comparability limitations (e.g., minimal-phenotyping UKB-derived definitions; portability-framework scores; treatment-specific or non-disease endpoints). PGS003333 is best supported because its phenotyping_reported is directly "Major Depressive Disorder" (high endpoint fidelity), it uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS-auto) with large genome-wide variant coverage (~1.09M), and it is developed from a disease-focused multi-cohort set (23andMe/PGC/UKB) rather than a portability framework; it also reports a reasonable disease-prediction metric (Nagelkerke pseudo-R2=0.022) in a sizable EUR validation (n=34,703), without explicit heavy clinical covariates (covariates listed as Unknown, which lowers confidence but is not an explicit leakage signal).

Runners-up: PGS003580 is from the same coherent MDD-focused study family with direct MDD endpoint and slightly higher reported R2 (0.0254) but is a PRSice-2 clumping/thresholding-style pipeline (structurally weaker than genome-wide shrinkage for highly polygenic traits) and comes from a preprint family with multiple near-clones, making it harder to identify a single clearly superior sibling from visible evidence. PGS002759 is also a strong direct-match candidate with a modern shrinkage method (PRS-CS) and a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.26, EUR eval n=39,444), but it lacks comparable R2/AUC reporting in the visible fields, limiting confidence versus PGS003333.

Key limitation driving DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL: no candidate provides clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2) in the visible evidence, and several candidates show non-comparable endpoints (e.g., muscle pain in fluoxetine takers; brain imaging traits) or framework/portability archetypes, so the top choice remains somewhat uncertain.

All 8 candidates are direct matches to dilated cardiomyopathy by trait_efo, with endpoint fidelity differences mainly in phenotyping_reported (generic DCM vs non-ischemic DCM vs clinical DCM). While full-model AUROC is not a PRS-only metric, the covariate set is basic (less risk of clinical leakage), making the reported performance more interpretable than if biomarker-heavy.

Runner-up PGS004861 is the non-MTAG sibling from the same publication with essentially identical endpoint/covariates/validation context but slightly weaker reported AUROC (0.70) and OR (1.56).

Main limitation: across the set, most metrics are full-model and not directly PRS-only comparable; additionally, several candidates are evaluated in MAE-only cohorts (PGS004946-004949) or have phenotype qualifiers (non-ischemic/clinical) that introduce endpoint heterogeneity, so the ranking relies on a combination of endpoint fidelity, MTAG preference, and the most interpretable available performance/effect-size signals rather than a clean head-to-head PRS-only benchmark. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to diverticular disease (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported align to diverticular disease/K57/diverticulitis). All 7 candidates are direct matches for a hyperthyroidism target via either explicit hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis endpoints (PGS001042/PGS001043/PGS001815/PGS002023) or the clinically dominant subtype Graves’ disease (PGS005264/PGS005265/PGS005266), which the provided domain_knowledge explicitly treats as a strong direct match for generic hyperthyroidism when competing alternatives are older UKB framework/portability scores.

All four candidates are direct matches to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy by trait_efo, but they differ in endpoint fidelity, method strength, and how comparable the reported performance is to a standalone PRS.

Among the two near-clone 2025 PRS-CS models, the MTAG version is mildly preferred per provided domain guidance (MTAG is a legitimate power-boost, not an endpoint mismatch) and it also shows stronger reported discrimination/effect evidence within the same covariate setting (full-model AUROC 0.8 vs 0.73; R² 0.048 vs 0.031; OR 1.33 vs 1.26; HR 2.34 vs 1.97). Direct HCM phenotype, but it is a sparse GWAS-hits score (27 variants) and the only visible AUROC is a full-model AUROC (0.821) with substantial clinical covariates (obesity, HTN, AF, CAD, plus rare-variant carrier status), which the domain guidance flags as non-comparable to PRS-only performance; thus its apparent AUROC advantage is heavily discounted despite large validation n.

A key limitation is covariate comparability: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric and includes thyroid biomarkers (TSH, T4, anti-TPO), which domain guidance flags as near-outcome covariates that can inflate AUROC and reduce PRS-only interpretability; no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided here.

Runners-up: PGS004935 is endpoint-faithful (Hypothyroidism), UKB-based, reports full-model AUROC=0.70 and OR=1.5 with EUR evaluation; despite smaller validation (n=8,417) and unknown covariates, it provides cleaner PRS-signal evidence via OR≈1.5 without explicit biomarker adjustment. PGS002766 is also endpoint-faithful (Hypothyroidism), uses PRS-CS with EUR evaluation and reports OR=1.47 (tight CI) in a disease-comparison study; it lacks AUC/R2 but has strong effect-size evidence and no explicit biomarker covariates. Confidence is Moderate because the top candidate’s headline AUROC is likely covariate-inflated and many other candidates lack PRS-only metrics, making benchmark transfer ranking uncertain.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to the same trait_efo and have the same phenotyping_reported: "Disorders of iron metabolism"), so this is a direct-match selection. Both models come from the same UKB portability publication, with identical training cohort (UKB), training n (391,124), validation sample size (19,883), covariates (basic demographics + PCs), and multi-ancestry evaluation distribution; thus endpoint fidelity and transportability context do not differentiate them. The only visible performance signal is partial correlation (partial-r), where PGS002031 is slightly higher (0.1355 vs 0.1307) with overlapping CIs, so the advantage is modest. Given the domain guidance that, when PRS-only AUC/R2 are absent, structural/method signals and available comparable metrics can be used as fallback, PGS002031 is preferred because it uses LDpred2 (genome-wide shrinkage) and includes substantially more variants (6713 vs 654), consistent with capturing more polygenic signal. Confidence is not high because both candidates are near-clones from the same framework/portability study and lack stronger PRS-comparable metrics (no AUC/R2/effect sizes), making the ranking reliant on modest partial-r and method/variant-count heuristics.

Direct-match candidates are present, but only one (PGS000114) directly targets the umbrella endpoint “Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis” in trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported; the other three are explicit JIA subtypes (enthesitis-related, oligoarticular, RF-negative polyarticular), which are less endpoint-aligned for a generic JIA target. All four models come from the same disease-focused publication family, use the same method (SparSNP), have the same EUR-only DEV/EVAL ancestry context, and use only basic covariates (sex, PCs 1–10), so the main differentiators are endpoint fidelity and the limited performance evidence available. Although subtype models report higher full-model AUROC (notably PGS000324 at 0.93), domain guidance cautions against treating full-model AUROC as PRS-only evidence; with no PGS-only AUC/R2 reported for any candidate, the safest benchmark-transfer bet is the most phenotype-aligned umbrella JIA score (PGS000114). Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS000325 (oligoarticular JIA) has stronger reported full-model AUROC (0.80) and OR per SD (1.93) than PGS000326 (AUROC 0.76; OR 1.51), while PGS000324 is deprioritized despite very high AUROC because it is a narrower subtype endpoint and the AUROC is full-model (potentially covariate-inflated) rather than PRS-only.

All 10 listed candidates are direct matches to kidney cancer (including renal carcinoma / renal cell carcinoma, which is explicitly noted in the provided domain knowledge as the clinically dominant subtype of kidney cancer). Among them, PGS004908 has the strongest visible PRS-relevant performance evidence: it reports the highest AUROC (0.74, albeit as a full-model metric) and a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.5, 95% CI 1.43–1.58), with covariates that are standard epidemiologic adjustments (age, sex, PCs, BMI, smoking, hypertension) rather than obvious clinical risk-calculator packaging. The runners-up are PGS000076 and PGS000787: both are endpoint-faithful (incident kidney cancer / renal cell carcinoma), use the same 19-variant genome-wide-significant set, and show similar full-model discrimination (AUROC ~0.722) with similar covariates; PGS000787 is explicitly derived from PGS000076 (inverse weights), so they form a coherent high-support cluster but do not exceed PGS004908’s stronger OR and higher AUROC. Main limitation: across the pool, PRS-only (covariate-free) AUC/R² is not reported, so comparisons rely on effect sizes and full-model metrics that may be covariate-influenced; this keeps confidence at Moderate despite PGS004908’s stronger visible signals.

Direct-match candidates for the target EFO concept (kidney failure) are present (PGS000708, PGS004492, PGS004562). Among these, PGS004562 is best supported as a likely benchmark-transfer winner because it targets the same kidney-failure endpoint (N18 chronic renal failure; trait_efo=kidney failure), uses a multi-score aggregation method (RFDiseasemetaPRS; domain guidance: ensembles/multi-score aggregation tend to outperform single-score construction), and shows a stronger per-SD effect size (OR=1.39548) than the other kidney-failure-labeled options (PGS004492 OR=1.1708; PGS000708 HR=1.19). The main limitation is that PGS004562 reports no PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and has unknown covariates, so the evidence is incomplete and confidence cannot be high.

Runners-up: (1) PGS002237 is not kidney-failure-labeled but is a very close direct clinical endpoint in the same disease spectrum (CKD stage 3+; eGFR<45) from a disease-focused PRS paper with strong reported discrimination (full-model AUROC=0.78) and moderate effect size (OR=1.47), making it a plausible benchmark-strong alternative despite heavier covariates. (2) PGS004492 is the closest like-for-like comparator to the best model (same N18 chronic renal failure endpoint and same study family) but is structurally weaker than PGS004562 (single-score LDpred2 vs metaPRS ensemble; smaller OR).

All 7 candidates are direct matches to knee osteoarthritis (trait_efo aligns), but most lack PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) and rely on effect sizes or full-model metrics, limiting certainty. PGS002767 is preferred because it is endpoint-faithful (phenotyping_reported: knee osteoarthritis) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,052,275 variants) with a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.35, CI 1.3–1.4), which the provided domain guidance treats as a meaningful predictor when AUC/R² are absent. As runners-up, PGS004549 and PGS004479 share the same knee OA endpoint family (gonarthrosis), are genome-wide (1,059,939 variants), and report similar moderate per-SD ORs (1.3667 and 1.3233, respectively); PGS004549 ranks above PGS004479 due to the slightly stronger reported OR. Key limitation: the top candidate lacks PRS-only AUROC/R² and the alternatives include a pan-trait sparse UKB framework score (PGS001192) and a GWAS-hits clinical model with only full-model AUROC (PGS002729), making cross-model performance comparability weak and keeping confidence below high. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 5 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo, but they differ materially on endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS000054 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused LOAD PRS study with a clear per-SD effect size (OR=1.73, 95% CI 1.57–1.93), which the provided domain guidance treats as strong discriminative evidence when AUC/R2 are missing; its covariates are basic (age, sex), reducing concern about covariate-driven inflation. Main limitation: it is evaluated in AMR (Hispanic/Latin American) only, while the target context and heritability reference are EUR; this ancestry mismatch lowers certainty about benchmark transfer.

Runner-up PGS000053 is essentially the EUR-evaluated sibling from the same publication with the same endpoint framing and covariates, but it has a weaker per-SD OR (1.29), suggesting weaker PRS signal despite better ancestry alignment. Second runner-up PGS000334 has a direct LO Alzheimer’s disease endpoint and EUR evaluation, and reports an R²=0.191; however, this appears to be a full-model/unspecified R² from a C+T score with unknown covariates and is far above the provided local h2_liability (~0.0269) ceiling sanity-check, making the metric likely non-comparable or inflated, so it cannot be relied upon as stronger PRS evidence. PGS002289 is deprioritized due to phenotype mismatch (cognition-by-age interaction rather than AD diagnosis performance), and PGS004918 is deprioritized due to very small development/validation (n=439 training; n=136 validation) and reliance on full-model AUROC only (0.731) with unknown covariates, which is not a valid substitute for PRS-only performance.

All listed candidates are direct matches to lung cancer (or very near-synonyms like lung/bronchus cancer), so selection hinges on endpoint fidelity plus PRS-comparable performance evidence and transportability signals. PGS000078 is preferred because it targets incident lung cancer, is evaluated in a very large European cohort (n=392,539), and reports a per-SD HR (1.16, 95% CI 1.11–1.22), providing PRS-specific signal beyond full-model discrimination; its covariate set is extensive (includes smoking variables, PM2.5, and family history), which makes the reported full-model AUROC (0.846) less PRS-comparable, but the effect-size evidence and coherent disease-focused multi-cohort context still make it the best-supported choice in this pool. Runner-up PGS000789 is essentially the same 109-variant score (explicitly derived from PGS000078) with very similar metrics (AUROC 0.846; HR 1.17) and similarly heavy covariates, so it remains highly competitive but offers no clear advantage over the original record from the same evidence cluster. Second runner-up PGS004860 shows the highest reported full-model AUROC (0.893) and OR (1.33) in a European evaluation, but it is supported by a much smaller validation sample (n=24,012) and still lacks PRS-only metrics; given domain guidance to discount covariate-inflated full-model AUROC and avoid over-weighting single-study outliers, it ranks behind the large, repeatedly supported 109-variant incident-lung-cancer cluster. Overall confidence is moderate because most candidates report only full-model AUROC (often with substantial non-genetic covariates) and essentially no PRS-only AUROC/R2, limiting direct comparability across models. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 12 visible candidates are direct matches to lupus erythematosus via trait_efo/trait_reported (mostly systemic lupus erythematosus; two are lupus erythematosus umbrella). However, most reported discrimination is full-model AUROC (not PRS-only), and one apparent top AUROC (PGS003960, 0.89) is explicitly adjusted by a “phenotype risk score”, which domain guidance flags as severe leakage/non-comparable packaging—so it is discounted despite high AUROC.

Best pick: PGS002082 (LDpred2; 361,553 variants) has strong structural support for external benchmark transfer: genome-wide shrinkage with very large variant count, and an endpoint aligned to the target umbrella (“Lupus (localized and systemic)”). It also reports a PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation 0.0212 with CI) rather than only a covariate-inflated full-model AUROC, and its evaluation spans multiple ancestries (AFR/EAS/EUR/GME/SAS), which is supportive for robustness.

Runners-up: PGS000754 (lassosum; 293,684 variants) is another genome-wide shrinkage score with large variant count and a direct SLE endpoint; despite only a modest full-model AUROC (0.65) and mixed-ancestry evaluation, its method/coverage make it a plausible high-transfer performer. PGS001870 is the sibling portability-framework score (penalized regression; 87 variants) with the same endpoint as PGS002082 but weaker PRS-comparable metric (partial-r 0.0184) and much sparser variant set, so it ranks behind.

Main limitation: no candidate provides clean PRS-only AUROC/R2 for the core SLE diagnosis endpoint; several candidates are subtype- or restricted-endpoint (e.g., early-onset, renal/nephritis) or have unknown covariates, and the strongest-looking AUROC is confounded by phenotype-risk covariate packaging. This keeps confidence below High. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple models mapped to lymphoid leukemia / lymphocytic leukemia, plus closely related chronic lymphocytic leukemia models). PGS000788 is best supported within the visible list because it has strong endpoint fidelity for the target (phenotyping_reported: Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia; trait_efo: lymphoid leukemia), uses a reasonably sized variant set (75), and shows comparatively strong per-SD effect size evidence (HR=1.7) alongside basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs) and large European evaluation (n=391,338). Main limitation: its reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics (not explicitly PRS-only), and it is a framework-style derivative of PGS000077 with inverse weights, so the apparent performance advantage could be driven by modeling/packaging rather than a cleaner standalone PRS signal.

Runners-up: PGS000077 is the closest sibling with the same incident lymphocytic leukemia endpoint and identical variant count (75) and similarly clean covariates, but with weaker effect size (HR=1.45) and slightly lower full-model AUROC/C-index. For a third-place alternative, PGS000648 (chronic lymphocytic leukemia) has strong discrimination evidence within its family (full_model_auc=0.696; OR per SD=2.124) and clean basic covariates, but it is a subtype endpoint (chronic) rather than the broader lymphoid leukemia target, and its metrics are also full-model rather than PRS-only, lowering certainty. Overall confidence is Moderate because no candidate provides clearly PRS-only comparable metrics, and several candidates are close with differing endpoint scope (lymphocytic vs chronic lymphocytic vs lymphoid leukemia). | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 7 candidates are direct matches by trait label, but they differ materially in endpoint fidelity and study archetype. PGS004606 is best supported because it is a disease-focused AMD score with a direct clinical endpoint (phenotyping_reported: "Age-related macular degeneration"), basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS; ~1.0M variants), and it reports a full-model AUROC=0.71 plus a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.76, 95% CI 1.73–1.78) in a large EUR evaluation (n=163,011). This combination (endpoint fidelity + strong effect size + disease-focused context) is the most coherent evidence package for likely external benchmark transfer.

Runner-up PGS004952 has an apparently much higher AUROC, but the visible AUROC is internally inconsistent (classification_metrics AUROC listed as 84.2 rather than 0.842) and it is for a narrower endpoint ("Late age-related macular degeneration") with a much smaller validation sample (n=1,232); despite clean/basic covariates, the metric anomaly and small eval size reduce confidence in it as the top pick. Runner-up PGS004607 is from the same 2024 Nat Genet family and has the same clean endpoint/covariates and large EUR evaluation (n=163,011), but shows weaker reported performance/effect size (AUROC=0.65; OR=1.48) and has a GWAS ancestry listed as AFR-only, which is a mild transportability concern relative to the EUR-based sibling.

Confidence is Moderate because most other candidates lack PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUC/R2) and two older UKB framework/portability scores (PGS001013, PGS001834, PGS002041) provide limited transferable evidence despite having some metrics/partial-r; the decision therefore relies heavily on endpoint fidelity + effect-size evidence from the Nat Genet disease-focused family.

Direct-match melanoma candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=melanoma and melanoma phenotyping). Among the visible set, PGS002247 is best supported for likely external benchmark performance because it targets an endpoint-faithful phenotype (incident invasive melanoma), reports comparatively strong discrimination evidence (full_model AUROC 0.691 with R² 0.072), and comes from an independent evaluation study explicitly focused on melanoma PRS (reducing framework/portability concerns). The two strongest runners-up from the same evaluation family are PGS002246 (same endpoint/study, very similar AUROC 0.688 and R² 0.07) and PGS002253 (same endpoint/study but weaker reported AUROC 0.662 and R² 0.051). Confidence is Moderate because the key reported metrics are full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), covariate sets differ across studies, and there exist other direct-match candidates with higher full-model AUROC but with heavier clinical covariates and/or smaller validation samples, making cross-study metric comparability uncertain.

All 6 candidates are nominally direct-match on trait_reported/trait_efo, but endpoint fidelity differs: PGS003450 is internally inconsistent (phenotyping_reported = Chronic lymphocytic leukemia despite trait_reported = Multiple myeloma), so it is penalized heavily versus the coherent multiple-myeloma endpoints of the others. Among the coherent MM candidates, none reports PRS-only AUROC/R2; the visible AUROCs are full-model and thus only weakly comparable across studies/covariate sets. Still, PGS002281 (Eur J Hum Genet 2022) shows the strongest reported discrimination signal in the pool with full_model AUROC=0.644 (CI 0.622–0.666) and a strong stratification metric (OR highest vs lowest quintiles = 3.18, CI 2.34–4.33) with basic covariates (age, sex, geographic region), making it the best-supported direct-match pick from the visible evidence. Runner-up PGS002306 reports an even higher full_model AUROC=0.69 but on a very small validation sample (n=290) with unknown covariates, making its apparent advantage less reliable. Next, within the PRSweb cluster (same publication family, similar basic covariates), PGS000653 (GWAS Hits; n=2,738 eval) slightly edges PGS000654/PGS000652 by marginally higher full_model AUROC (0.577) and per-SD OR (1.327). Overall confidence is Moderate because key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2, incremental AUROC) are missing across candidates, and full-model AUROC differences may be covariate-driven; heritability is provided only as a ceiling/sanity check and cannot resolve these comparability gaps.

All 7 visible candidates are direct matches to multiple sclerosis by trait_efo and (except PGS001271) have phenotype fields consistent with a generic MS diagnosis endpoint. PGS002726 is preferred because it is disease-focused (IMSGC), endpoint-aligned (phenotyping_reported: Multiple sclerosis), and shows the strongest visible discrimination signal among the set (full-model AUROC=0.80 with a high top-decile OR=15.0), suggesting strong PRS stratification even though PRS-only metrics are not provided. The main limitation is that its covariates are unknown and the validation sample is small (n=938), so the reported AUROC may not be directly comparable and external-benchmark transfer is uncertain.

Runners-up: PGS002038 (LDpred2, genome-wide shrinkage with very large variant count and a UKB-derived portability framework context; partial-r=0.0396 provides some PRS-comparable signal but no AUROC/R2) is structurally strong and likely to transfer reasonably, but lacks richer disease-focused validation metrics here. PGS000809 is a disease-focused multi-cohort MS clumping score with a moderate variant count and reports full-model AUROC=0.765 plus R²=0.069 and a beta effect size; however, these are not explicitly PRS-only metrics and the method is less powerful than genome-wide shrinkage, making it a slightly weaker bet than PGS002038 for a hidden benchmark.

Direct-match candidates for myocardial infarction are present (multiple models with trait_efo=myocardial infarction or acute myocardial infarction). Among these, the strongest visible direct-match support comes from the 2024 HGG Adv MVP-derived MI (PheCode 411.2) models, which are disease-endpoint aligned (phenotyping_reported: Myocardial infarction), use genome-wide shrinkage/continuous methods (ldpred/prscs/prscsx) with very large variant counts (~1.27–1.29M), and report strong effect-size evidence (several OR per SD ≥1.5) alongside C-index values ~0.78 in European validation. Within that coherent family, PGS005039 has the highest reported C-index (0.784836989...) and a strong OR per SD (1.578, 95% CI 1.5–1.67), making it the best-supported pick from the visible evidence.

Runners-up are selected from the same high-support MI PheCode family: PGS005035 (C-index 0.783355..., OR 1.541) and PGS005045 (C-index 0.783850..., OR 1.554) are extremely close on both discrimination and effect size. Other direct-match MI candidates (e.g., UKB pan-trait sparse snpnet scores PGS001314–PGS001317) have explicit PGS-only metrics but come from a known pan-trait sparse framework and show much weaker PRS-only AUROC (~0.58–0.60) and/or smaller PRS-only R2, which domain guidance flags as less reliable for external transfer than disease-focused, genome-wide shrinkage scores. Acute MI ICD10 I21 models (PGS004458/PGS004528) have endpoint alignment but provide only single OR estimates with unknown covariates and no comparable PRS-only metrics, limiting confidence.

Main limitation: the MVP MI PheCode models are near-clones with very small metric differences and only European-selected validation shown, so the top-1 vs top-2 ordering is uncertain and confidence is reduced despite strong overall direct-match evidence.

Both visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are J33 nasal polyp), come from the same publication, use the same training cohort (UKB), have identical ancestry distribution (DEV/EVAL EUR only), identical variant count (1,059,939), and have similarly limited reporting (no PRS-comparable AUC/R2; covariates listed as Unknown). With endpoint fidelity and study context effectively tied, the main differentiator is the reported per-SD effect size: PGS004535 reports a stronger OR (1.600668) than PGS004465 (1.3496), and domain guidance treats OR≥1.5 as a strong discriminative-power signal when AUC/R2 are absent. Confidence is not High because the covariate set is unknown for both and there are no PRS-only discrimination metrics to confirm that the higher OR translates to better benchmark transfer; additionally, method differences (RFDiseasemetaPRS vs LDpred2) cannot be fully interpreted from the visible metadata alone.

Both visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = nicotine dependence; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported = Tobacco use disorder) and come from the same UKB portability publication with the same training cohort (UKB), training N (391,124), and similar basic covariates, so endpoint fidelity and study context do not differentiate them. The main differentiator is the comparable reported PRS metric: PGS002037 shows higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0741, CI 0.0601–0.0881) than PGS001830 (0.0557, CI 0.0416–0.0697), suggesting stronger standalone signal in the selected European validation record. Method/structure also mildly favors PGS002037 (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage; 847,691 variants) over PGS001830 (penalized regression; 13,838 variants) as a general external-performance signal when endpoints are otherwise identical. Confidence is only Moderate because both models are from a portability/framework-style paper (a known generalization risk per provided domain guidance) and the only visible performance evidence is partial-r (no PRS-only AUC/R2), limiting how decisively we can separate near-sibling models.

All 7 candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target concept (nodular goiter), but they split into two endpoint families: (i) UKB portability-framework scores for “Nontoxic multinodular goiter” (PGS001814, PGS002022) with only weak partial-correlation evidence and no AUC/R2/OR; and (ii) a disease-focused multi-cohort thyroid/benign thyroid disease study family (PGS005261–PGS005263) that directly targets “Benign nodular goiter” and reports effect sizes plus full-model AUROC (not PRS-only). Per the provided domain guidance, phenotype alignment plus disease-focused multi-cohort context and effect-size evidence typically outrank portability-framework partial-r when endpoint fidelity is acceptable.

PGS005262 is selected as best because it is an endpoint-faithful benign nodular goiter score from the coherent multi-cohort family and, within that family, it has the strongest visible discrimination/effect evidence (highest full-model AUROC among benign-goiter models: 0.5933; and the largest reported per-SD OR: 1.408) using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) with very large variant count (~1.085M), a positive structural signal versus the sparse P+T model.

Runners-up: PGS005263 is the closest sibling (same endpoint family, same method, similar variant count) with slightly weaker AUROC/OR; PGS005261 is third as it remains endpoint-faithful but uses a sparse P+T approach with far fewer variants (110) and weaker effect evidence. Main limitation lowering confidence: for the 2026 multi-cohort models, covariates are “Unknown” and the only AUROC shown is full-model (not PRS-only), so comparability of the reported AUROC across candidates is limited; nonetheless, the effect-size and structural signals still favor the PRSCS benign-goiter models over the UKB portability partial-r scores.

All 10 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (obesity) via trait_efo=obesity, but most lack PRS-comparable performance metrics, making the ranking evidence-limited.

Best pick: PGS002033 is preferred because it provides the strongest directly PRS-comparable performance signal in the visible set (partial correlation partial-r=0.0789 in European validation) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (846,292). However, it comes from a UK Biobank portability/framework-style paper (“Portability of 245 polygenic scores…”), which domain guidance flags as tending to underperform disease-focused models in external benchmarks; this keeps the overall outcome at DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL.

Runner-up 1: PGS001298 has explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.5757; PGS-only R²=0.01146) plus incremental AUROC reported, and includes multi-ancestry evaluation. But it is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”) and uses a sparse snpnet model (9,227 variants), both warning signals for external transfer.

Runner-up 2: PGS005235 is endpoint-faithful despite the broader label (“Adiposity”) because phenotyping_reported is an obesity phecode endpoint, and it uses LDpred2-auto with a large variant count (709,828) and multi-cohort GWAS sources listed (EGG, GIANT, UKB). Its limitation is that it reports only an OR (no PRS-only AUROC/R²), so comparability to the benchmark is less certain than for candidates with PRS-comparable metrics.

Other candidates were deprioritized mainly due to weaker/less comparable evidence: PGS001825 has lower partial-r than PGS002033; PGS003400/PGS003959 are GW-significant SNP sets with limited comparable metrics; PGS004447/PGS004517 have only ORs with unclear covariates; PGS005145/PGS005154 are EAS-evaluated only (less robust if benchmark ancestry is not EAS). | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, but the pool is dominated by framework-style UKB-derived scores and several newer models with only effect-size summaries and no PRS-comparable AUROC/R2, limiting a clearly high-quality pick.

Best pick: PGS001274 is preferred because it provides explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.57595; PGS R2 no covariates=0.00945) plus incremental AUROC (0.00777) under basic covariates, and it is a direct osteoporosis endpoint (TTE osteoporosis without pathological fracture). Among the candidates with PRS-only metrics, it has stronger PRS-only R2 and AUROC than its closest sibling (PGS001273), and its PRS-only R2 is well below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.584), passing the sanity check.

Runner-up 1: PGS001273 is the closest competitor with similarly clean, PRS-only metrics and the most endpoint-generic phenotyping_reported (“Osteoporosis”), but it has weaker PRS-only AUROC (0.5685) and PRS-only R2 (0.00688) than PGS001274.

Runner-up 2: PGS002768 is a direct osteoporosis score using PRS-CS with a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.31, 95% CI 1.25–1.38) and a reasonably large evaluation sample (n=39,444). It is ranked behind the snpnet models because it lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 in the visible record, making benchmark transfer harder to infer.

Main limitation driving DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL: the top two metric-bearing candidates (PGS001274/PGS001273) come from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused models in external validation; meanwhile, the more recent disease-focused-looking candidates (e.g., Commun Biol 2024 and Commun Biol 2025) provide only single effect-size points with unknown/limited covariate and discrimination reporting, preventing a high-confidence selection. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to trait_efo=otosclerosis). PGS002046 is preferred because its endpoint is the generic disease label (phenotyping_reported: "Otosclerosis") rather than a time-to-event formulation, and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (570,308), which is a positive structural signal for external performance relative to a sparse pan-trait UKB score. Its reported PRS-comparable metric is partial correlation (partial-r=0.0182 in EUR), which is limited but at least directly PRS-oriented.

Main limitation: both candidates come from UK Biobank framework-style papers ("across 813 traits" sparse snpnet; "Portability of 245 polygenic scores"), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused models; additionally, PGS002046 lacks AUROC/R² and effect sizes, so the performance evidence is sparse and makes the choice only moderately confident.

Runner-up: PGS001255 has explicit PRS-only AUROC (0.6319) and PRS-only R² (0.01341) plus a full-model AUROC (0.6532) with basic covariates, but it is a sparse snpnet model from the "813 traits" pan-trait framework and uses a time-to-event endpoint ("TTE otosclerosis"), both of which are negative signals for general benchmark transfer versus a cleaner generic endpoint with genome-wide shrinkage.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (ovarian neoplasm) via ovarian cancer / malignant neoplasm of ovary / epithelial ovarian cancer endpoints. PGS000082 is best supported because it targets incident ovarian cancer with a large European evaluation (n=211,958) and reports the strongest discrimination among broadly comparable, non-horizon endpoints in this list (full-model AUROC ~0.656 / C-index ~0.655), coming from a large cross-cancer evaluation in two large cohorts; while full-model metrics are discounted, its performance is not an obvious outlier driven by heavy clinical biomarkers, and the endpoint is cleanly aligned. Runner-up PGS000793 uses the same endpoint/covariate structure and shows slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.66) but is explicitly a re-weighted derivative of PGS000082 (inverse weights), making it less clearly the primary transferable PRS despite similar evaluation context. Best pick: PGS002075 (Urinary calculus; LDpred2; 731,196 variants) from the UKB portability study. It has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Urinary calculus; trait_efo: urolithiasis) and provides a PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation 0.0385, CI 0.0246–0.0524), which is higher than the sibling penalized-regression score (PGS001864). Given the domain guidance that genome-wide shrinkage methods and stronger PRS-comparable metrics are supportive when endpoint fidelity is similar, this is the most supported choice among the visible set.

Runner-up 1: PGS001864 is the closest competitor (same endpoint, same study family, PRS-comparable partial-r reported) but has a lower partial-r (0.0323).

Runner-up 2: PGS001250 has direct endpoint alignment (TTE calculus of kidney and ureter) and reports explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.5668; PGS R² 0.00592) plus incremental AUROC, but it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework ("813 traits" snpnet) which the provided domain knowledge flags as tending to generalize poorly versus more disease-focused constructions; additionally its endpoint is time-to-event, which is a mild negative signal for a generic disease-risk target.

The two 2024 models (PGS004493/PGS004563) are direct matches but are less supportable here because they report only an OR (1.23–1.28) with unknown covariates and no PRS-comparable AUROC/R², making them hard to rank against candidates with clearer PRS-only/PRS-comparable metrics.

Direct-match candidates for uterine cancer are present, but the pool mixes umbrella uterine-cancer labels with endometrial-carcinoma endpoints and most records lack PRS-only AUROC/R2, limiting certainty.

Best pick: PGS003381. It targets the clinically dominant uterine cancer subtype (uterine endometrial carcinoma; trait_efo=endometrial carcinoma; phenotyping_reported matches) and uses a genome-wide method (lassosum) with a large variant count (529,365). It also reports relatively strong full-model discrimination (AUROC 0.761) and an R²=0.11, though these are not explicitly PRS-only metrics, so they are supportive but not definitive.

Runner-up 1: PGS001795. Exact label alignment (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported uterine cancer) and a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto; 911,692 variants) are strong structural signals. However, it comes from a global biobank framework-style paper and its PRS-comparable signal is small (pgs_only_r2=0.001948), consistent with the low heritability ceiling noted for uterine cancer (h2_liability≈0.0116), which tempers expectations.

Runner-up 2: PGS000541. Exact mapped trait (malignant neoplasm of uterus; trait_efo=uterine cancer; phenotyping_reported matches) and disease-focused cancer-PRS repository context are supportive, with moderate per-SD OR evidence (OR 1.311). But it is a sparse GWAS-hits score (18 variants) with modest AUROC (0.576), making it less likely to top an external benchmark than the genome-wide endometrial-carcinoma model.
